title: How to Enable MMS Messaging & Fix Download Issues on Android
summary: MMS not working on Android? Learn how to enable MMS messaging, fix download issues, and troubleshoot common problems with our step-by-step guide.
body_markdown:
## How to Enable MMS Messaging & Fix Download Issues on Android


To enable MMS messaging on Android, open the Google Messages app, tap your profile icon in the top-right corner, go to Messages settings → Advanced, and toggle on Auto-download MMS. You must also ensure Mobile data is turned on in your phone's Settings → Network & internet (or Connections), as MMS cannot download over standard Wi-Fi alone.


Whether you're wondering where MMS settings are on Android, seeing a "Failed to download multimedia message" error on Samsung or Google Pixel, or getting a "Multimedia message not supported by network" alert, follow the steps below to turn on MMS and fix download issues.


## How to enable MMS on Android


Where MMS settings live on Android depends on whether you're adjusting your messaging app (Google Messages or Samsung Messages) or your phone's cellular carrier settings. Check both below:


### 1. Turn on Auto-download MMS in Google Messages (Pixel, Motorola, and Modern Samsung)


1.


Open the Google Messages app on your Android phone.


2.


Tap your profile picture or initial in the top-right corner and select Messages settings. (On older versions, tap the three-dot menu → Settings.)


3.


Tap Advanced at the bottom of the menu.


4.


Toggle on Auto-download MMS (and Auto-download MMS when roaming if you travel frequently).


### 2. Enable MMS on Samsung Galaxy (Samsung Messages)


If your Galaxy phone uses the Samsung Messages app instead of Google Messages:


1.


Open Samsung Messages and tap the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.


2.


Tap Settings → More settings → Multimedia messages.


3.


Toggle on Auto retrieve (and Auto retrieve while roaming if needed).


### 3. Enable Mobile Data & Verify APN Settings (Device Settings)


1.


**Open settings:** Start by opening the Settings app on your Android device.


2.


**Network and internet:** Scroll down and tap on Network & internet (on Pixel/Motorola) or Connections (on Samsung Galaxy).


3.


**Mobile network:** Select Mobile network (or SIMs) to access cellular settings, and ensure Mobile data is turned On, as MMS requires an active cellular data connection.


4.


**Access Point Names (APN):** Tap on Access Point Names (under Advanced or Mobile Network). If MMS is not working or you just switched carriers (such as Visible, Mint, or Cricket), it might be due to incorrect APN settings. Tap the three-dot menu → Reset to default, or verify your carrier's MMSC and MMS proxy settings on their support page.


5.


**Activate MMS:** If you see an APN type field inside your active APN, make sure mm is listed.


Once these settings are correctly configured, your device should be ready to send and receive MMS messages.


## How to download MMS messages from Android


If Auto-download MMS is turned off—or you have a weak cellular connection—incoming picture and group texts appear as a downloadable attachment bubble instead of opening automatically. Here is how to manually download and open MMS messages:


1.


**Open messaging app:** Launch Google Messages (or Samsung Messages) to view the message you want to download.


2.


**Locate the MMS:** Find the conversation thread containing the unopened MMS message.


3.


**Tap to download image/video:** Tap the Download icon (downward arrow) inside the message bubble. Make sure Mobile data is turned on while it downloads.


4.


**Save to gallery:** Once downloaded, tap the image or video to open it full-screen, then tap the Save icon (or three-dot menu → Save) This action will store the media in your phone's Gallery or Google Photos.


## Why aren't MMS messages downloading or sending?


Now what if you followed all the steps above and MMS messages still won’t download? MMS is an older carrier-dependent method for sending multimedia over text messages, and it doesn’t always work as smoothly as RCS or newer messaging apps. Because MMS routes through your carrier's Multimedia Messaging Service Center (MMSC) over cellular data, not standard Wi-Fi, anything that interrupts your mobile data session, carrier provisioning, or file size limits can stop a picture or group message from downloading.


## How to fix MMS issues on Android (8 proven fixes)


### 1. Check the attachment size


First, check the size of the attachment that you want to send or receive. Often, your carrier will limit the MMS file size. Different carriers have different file size limits.


For example,[Verizon](https://www.verizon.com/support/knowledge-base-14641/) only allows images up to 1.2 MB and videos up to 3.5 MB, while T-Mobile has a 1 MB limit for sending (3 MB for receiving). Additionally, the recipient’s carrier can limit the file size. So even if your carrier supports a larger file size, if the recipient’s carrier doesn’t, it’ll reject or compress the file.


For maximum compatibility, ensure your attachment is less than 1 MB in size, then try sending or receiving it again.


### 2. Turn on mobile data (and temporarily turn off Wi-Fi)


Unlike standard SMS texts or RCS chats, MMS messages require an active cellular data connection to download—even when you are connected to Wi-Fi. Go to Settings → Network & internet (or Connections) → Mobile network and make sure Mobile data is turned On. If a picture is stuck downloading, temporarily toggle Wi-Fi Off so your phone is forced to pull the MMS over cellular data.


### 3. Toggle Auto-download MMS


If your MMS messages fail to download on an Android, it could be because the Auto-download MMS setting is stuck. In the Google Messages app, tap your profile icon → Messages settings → Advanced → Auto-download MMS. If the option is on, try turning it off and manually downloading your MMS message. However, if the option is off, try turning it on and seeing if the MMS message downloads automatically.


### 4. Fix "Multimedia message not supported by network" errors


If your Android says "Multimedia message not supported by network" or "Message not sent: service not activated on network," your carrier connection is blocking MMSC routing. Fix it with these three checks:


-


**Check your carrier plan and roaming settings:** Ensure your wireless plan includes MMS (prepaid plans and MVNOs like Visible or Mint occasionally require a manual APN refresh after activation) and turn on Data roaming if you are outside your home network.


-


**Turn off Wi-Fi Calling temporarily:** Some carriers block MMS packets over Wi-Fi Calling. Go to Settings → Network & internet → SIMs → Wi-Fi Calling, toggle it off, and retry the download.


-


**Reset APN settings:** Go to Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network → Access Point Names, tap the three-dot menu, and select Reset to default.


### 5. Fix "Failed to download multimedia message" on Samsung Galaxy


If you see "Failed to download multimedia message" on a Samsung phone, check for two Samsung-specific conflicts:


-


**Turn off Data Saver:** Go to Settings → Connections → Data usage → Data saver and make sure it is turned Off, as Data Saver restricts background MMS downloads.


-


**Check both messaging apps:** If you recently switched between Samsung Messages and Google Messages, open Settings → Apps → Choose default apps → SMS app and confirm only one app is set as your active default.


### 6. Check your network connection and Airplane Mode


A poor network connection is another possible reason for an MMS not sending or downloading. To check your mobile data connection, see if you have 2 or more signal bars. Toggle Airplane Mode On for 15 seconds, then turn it Off to force your phone to reconnect to the nearest cell tower.


### 7. Restart your phone


Restarting your phone can solve many temporary modem and carrier issues, so this is generally a good solution to try. Hold the Power button (or Power + Volume Up on newer Androids) until you see the power menu pop up, then select Restart. After the restart completes, check if you can send or receive your MMS message.


### 8. Clear cache (and check MMS Service) in the Messages app


Another possibility is that the Messages app has corrupted temporary files and can’t receive your messages. Try clearing the cache by going to Settings → Apps → Messages → Storage (or Storage & cache). Then, tap Clear cache. Avoid tapping Clear storage/data unless necessary, as it can reset app preferences.


If the issue persists, repeat the same Clear cache step for the system app named MMS Service (tap the three-dot menu in Settings → Apps → Show system apps → MMS Service → Storage → Clear cache).


## MMS resources for businesses


For businesses looking to engage[users over MMS](https://www.twilio.com/verify) , it’s helpful to gain a deeper understanding of what MMS is and how it differs from other protocols.


### What does MMS mean?


MMS is an extension of short message service (SMS), allowing the exchange of larger text messages (more than 160 characters), images, audio clips, and videos over a cellular network.


When a user sends an MMS message, the sending device must first encode the content before sending it to the[Multimedia Messaging Service Center](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-is-mms) (MMSC) of the sending device’s carrier. If the receiving device is on the same carrier, the MMSC sends the message directly to the receiving device. Otherwise, the MMSC sends it to the MMSC of the receiving device’s carrier, which forwards it to the receiving device.


Learn more about[MMS](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-is-mms) .


### What is group MMS?


Group MMS allows you to create group chats much like[SMS](https://www.twilio.com/sms) conversations, but over MMS. This allows for all members of the group to receive all messages sent to the group, not just the starter of the group. Doing so allows you to converse with 3 or more participants and keep everyone in the loop simultaneously.


The main advantage of group MMS over other messaging apps is that no additional app downloads are necessary, meaning anyone with a[mobile device](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/12427869273627-Twilio-Frontline-Limitation-of-New-Sales-Notice-and-Information) can join a group MMS.


Learn more about[how to use group texting](https://www.twilio.com/blog/group-texting-in-conversations) for business.


### SMS vs. MMS vs. other messaging apps


SMS is the most common choice for text messaging. That’s because SMS is a universal technology supported by every mobile network and device worldwide. It's also a clear choice for businesses because customers don’t have to download an additional app.


Apps such as[WhatsApp](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/messaging/channels/whatsapp) have clear advantages over MMS when sending media files. Whereas MMS can incur carrier costs above and beyond the data used, WhatsApp and other messaging apps are free to use—apart from the cost of data. Plus, WhatsApp has more features, such as group messaging and audio/video calling. Finally, as mentioned, file size limits on MMS can be restrictive and vary from carrier to carrier.


[RCS (Rich Communication Services)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/what-is-rcs-messaging) is the modern upgrade to SMS and MMS built directly into Google Messages on Android and Apple Messages on iOS 18+, offering high-resolution media, read receipts, and Wi-Fi messaging without strict 1 MB carrier limits, though phones still fall back to MMS when RCS is unavailable.


Other messaging apps are a “walled garden” chock-full of limitations. For example, WeChat users can only receive messages from WeChat users. So to communicate with users in those ecosystems, businesses must have a presence in each one, which requires additional developer time and effort.


Dive deeper into the different text messaging options with[What Are SMS and MMS and How Do They Differ?](https://www.twilio.com/learn/messaging/what-are-sms-and-mms)

## Frequently asked questions


### Why do I have to manually download MMS messages on Android?


You have to tap to download MMS messages when Auto-download MMS is turned off in your messaging app, when Mobile data is disabled, or when you are roaming outside your home network. To make pictures and group messages open automatically, open Google Messages → Profile icon → Messages settings → Advanced and turn on Auto-download MMS.


### What does "Multimedia message not supported by network" mean on Android?


This error means your phone cannot reach your wireless carrier's Multimedia Messaging Service Center (MMSC). It usually happens when Mobile data is switched off, your Access Point Name (APN) settings are misconfigured after switching carriers, or your prepaid plan does not have MMS provisioned.


### What is the MMS Service app on Android?


MMS Service is a built-in Android system process that handles sending and receiving multimedia messages in the background between your messaging app and your carrier's network. It is completely safe—if MMS messages get stuck downloading, clearing the cache for MMS Service in Settings → Apps → Show system apps can fix the issue.


### Why won't my Android download MMS messages automatically?


The most common culprit is the auto-download MMS setting. Go to your Google Messages app, tap your profile icon → Messages settings → Advanced → Auto-download MMS. Try toggling this setting—if it's on, turn it off and manually download messages. If it's off, turn it on to enable automatic downloads.


### What's the maximum file size for MMS messages?


File size limits vary by carrier. Verizon allows up to 1.2MB for images and 3.5MB for videos, while T-Mobile caps it at 1MB for sending. For best compatibility across all carriers, keep attachments under 1MB. If your file is too large, it won't send or the recipient's carrier might reject it.


### Do I need mobile data enabled to send MMS messages?


Yes, MMS requires an active data connection to work (unlike regular SMS text messages). Make sure mobile data is turned on in Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network. Even if you're connected to Wi-Fi, most Android devices still need mobile data enabled for MMS to function properly.


### Why do MMS messages work sometimes but not others?


Inconsistent MMS performance usually comes down to network signal strength or carrier issues. MMS needs a stronger connection than SMS, so weak signal areas can cause problems. Try moving to a location with better coverage or restart your phone to refresh the network connection.
